summary.en: Use addresses to reach live objects, distinguish a pointer from its target, and inspect pointers with %p.
summary.bn: অ্যাড্রেস দিয়ে ভেরিয়েবলে পৌঁছাও, পয়েন্টার আর তার টার্গেট আলাদা করে দেখো এবং %p দিয়ে অ্যাড্রেস প্রিন্ট করো।

notes: Object addresses, address-of and indirection are central C features from C89 onward. The examples target C17. NULL is used here for that baseline; C23 also introduces nullptr, discussed in the dedicated void and null pointer lesson.

examples.explanationHtml: Both expressions read the same marks object after the write, so both print 85.

examples.explanationHtml: The result is undefined: NULL selects no int object. Assign a live int address before writing through p.

practice.title: Change a caller value through a pointer
practice.statementHtml: Read one int from -100 to 100. Print Mark: then twice the input. Perform the change through an int pointer.
hints: Take the address after the variable exists.

practice.title: Choose one of two scores
practice.statementHtml: Read two ints from -100 to 100 and choice 0 or 1. Print Scores and choice: then the chosen score through a pointer.
hints: Both possible addresses belong to live elements.

practice.title: Demonstrate shared aliases
practice.statementHtml: Read two ints a and b from -100 to 100. Print Two integers (-100 to 100): then assign b through a pointer to a and print a plus the value observed through a copied pointer.
hints: A pointer copy shares the target rather than copying the target value.

practice.title: Select an optional target
practice.statementHtml: Read an int from -100 to 100 and a flag 0 or 1. Print Value and flag: then NONE for flag 0, otherwise increment through a selected pointer and print the result.
hints: Test the pointer before accessing its target.

quiz.prompt: For int x=7; int *p=&x;, what is stored in p?
quiz.explanation: The initializer takes x's address rather than reading its value.

quiz.prompt: What does *p = 9 change when p points to x?
quiz.explanation: Dereferencing selects the live target object.

quiz.prompt: What is the type of q in int *p, q;?
quiz.explanation: The star belongs to the declarator p; declare pointers separately for clarity.

quiz.prompt: Which initialized pointer is safe to compare with NULL before assignment?
quiz.explanation: Explicit NULL initialization avoids an indeterminate pointer value.

Does p=&b copy b into the previous target of p?

quiz.prompt: What behavior does dereferencing NULL have in C17?
quiz.explanation: NULL provides no object to access.

quiz.prompt: Which marks values are read after the pointer assignment?
quiz.explanation: The direct name and dereference select the same object.

quiz.prompt: What values remain after p is redirected but q writes through its old address?
quiz.explanation: q still aliases a, while p selects b.

quiz.explanation: The null state is checked before a later valid dereference.

examQuestions.question: Draw x, p and &p for int x=7; int *p=&x; and explain p versus *p.
examQuestions.answerHtml: x is an int object holding seven. p is a separate pointer object holding the address of x. *p accesses x; &p is the address of the pointer object, whose type is int **. Reassigning p changes its selected target, while assigning *p changes x.

examQuestions.question: Read an int from -100 to 100 and a flag 0 or 1. Print Value and flag: then NONE for flag 0, otherwise increment through a selected pointer and print the result.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int value, flag;
    puts("Value and flag:");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &value, &flag) != 2 || value < -100 || value > 100 ||
        flag < 0 || flag > 1) {
        return 1;
    }
    int *p = NULL;
    if (flag == 1) {
        p = &value;
    }
    if (p == NULL) {
        puts("NONE");
    } else {
        (*p)++;
        printf("%d\n", value);
    }
    return 0;
}

Test the pointer before accessing its target.
